source.publication: 2025 Maryland Resident Booklet (State and Local Tax Forms and Instructions), Form 502
source.section: Form 502 Lines 1, 7, 15-21; Instruction 16 standard deduction (PDF page 21); Instruction 10 and Exemption Amount Chart 10A (PDF pages 12-13); Instruction 17 Tax Rate Schedule I (PDF page 22); Instruction 10 'EXEMPTIONS ALLOWED' (PDF page 13): 1,000 for age 65 or older on the last day of the year; Form 502 Exemptions Line B

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 40,000.00 + interest 2,550.00 = 42,550.00. Federal taxable income = 42,550.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 24,800.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 502 Line 1 federal AGI 42,550.00; Lines 2-6 additions 0.00 (no non-Maryland municipal interest); Line 7 total 42,550.00. Line 14 two-income subtraction: 0.00 (not a joint return). Line 15 total subtractions 0.00. Line 16 Maryland AGI = 42,550.00 - 0.00 = 42,550.00. Line 17 standard deduction (Instruction 16, flat by filing status) = 3,350.00. Line 18 net income = 42,550.00 - 3,350.00 = 39,200.00. Line 19 exemptions: Chart 10A at federal AGI 42,550.00 (not over 100,000) gives 3,200.00 each x 1 (Box A) + 1,000.00 x 1 for age 65 or older (Box B, not reduced by the chart) = 4,200.00. Line 20 taxable net income = 39,200.00 - 4,200.00 = 35,000.00. Line 21 tax, Schedule I as numbers: 2.00% x 1,000.00 = 20.00 + 3.00% x 1,000.00 = 30.00 + 4.00% x 1,000.00 = 40.00 + 4.75% x 32,000.00 = 1,520.00; total 1,610.00. (The tax table row 35,000-35,050, PDF page 36, gives 1,611; expected keeps the formula figure.) Lines 22-26 credits: none modelled or claimed, 0.00; Maryland state tax 1,610.00. Local tax (Lines 28-33) out of scope; 2% capital gain tax (Line 21b) not charged (no gains, AGI under 350,000). The IRA distribution does not qualify for the pension exclusion (Line 10a: a traditional IRA does not qualify), so Line 10a is 0.00 and the 1,000 age exemption is the only age relief.
